Number of remaining triangles = 10

So, number of triangles in the given figure = 6 + 6 + 10 = 22

questions.q_en: Three different positions of the same dice are shown, the six faces of which have numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60. Which of the following statement is true?
options_en: Face having number '20' is opposite to face having number '10'.
Face having number '50' is opposite to face having number '30'.
Face having number '10' is opposite to face having number '60'.
Face having number '40' is opposite to face having number '20'.
questions.solution_en:
From the above given three different positions of the same dice, it can be concluded that,

· Face having number '50' is not opposite to the face with numbers 10, 20, 30 and 40 because these numbers are adjacent to the face with number '50'.

So, the face having number '50' is opposite to the face having number '60'.

· Face having number '10' is not opposite to the face with numbers 20, 50, and 40 because these numbers are adjacent to the face with number '10'.

So, the face having number '10' is opposite to the face having number '30'.

· Face having number '40' is not opposite to the face with numbers 10, 50, and 30 because these numbers are adjacent to the face with number '40'.

So, the face having number '40' is opposite to the face having number '20'.

Thus, the answer is option (d).

questions.q_en: January 1, 1977 was Thursday. What day of the week was January 1, 1978?
questions.solution_en:
The year 1977 was not a leap year. So, it had 1 odd day.

It is given that 1st day of the year 1977 is Thursday.

So, 1st day of the year 1978 is = Thursday + 1 day = Friday

Hence, it will be Friday.

questions.q_en:
The question below consists of two statements numbered I and II given below it. You have to decide whether the data given in the statements are sufficient to answer the questions.

Who is the tallest among five friends A, B, C, D and E?

Statement I: Only one person is taller than A. D is taller than B but not taller than E.

Statement II: C is taller than B. At least one person is taller than E.
options_en: If the data given in both statements I and II together are not sufficient to answer the question
If the data in statement II alone are sufficient to answer the question, while the data in statement I alone are not sufficient to answer the question
If the data in both statements I and II together are necessary to answer the question
If the data in statement I alone are sufficient to answer the question, while the data in statement II alone are not sufficient to answer the question
questions.solution_en:
It is given that,

Statement I,

Only one person is taller than A. D is taller than B but not taller than E.

Case 1,

E > A > D > B > C

Case 2,

E > A > D > C > B

Case 3,

E > A > C > D > B

Case 4,

C > A > E > D > B

We do not have further information. Hence statement I alone is not sufficient.

Statement II,

C is taller than B. At least one person is taller than E.

We do not have further information. Hence statement II alone is not sufficient.

From statements I and II,

Only one person is taller than A. D is taller than B but not taller than E.

C is taller than B. At least one person is taller than E.

We get,

C > A > E > D > B

Here, C is the tallest of all.

Hence, the data in both statements I and II together are necessary to answer the question.

He takes a final left turn, drives 18 km and stops at Point Q. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he now drive to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90° turns only.)
questions.solution_en:
Manish starts from Point A and drives 12 km towards East. He then takes a left turn, drives 5 km, turns left and drives 30 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 20 km. He takes a final left turn, drives 18 km and stops at Point Q.

So, he drives 15 km towards North to reach Point A again.
